newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to keep telco curbs, end Teleglobe monopoly.
newsitem.headline: Canada to keep telco curbs, end Teleglobe monopoly.

text.p: Canada has made an offer to the WTO negotiations on telecommunications which would maintain its restrictions on foreign ownership of telephone companies, a government statement said on Tuesday.

The offer, made at the World Trade Organization in Geneva, would, if accepted, end Teleglobe Inc's monopoly on overseas traffic by October 1, 1998, and completely liberalize the carriage of international traffic by the end of 1999.
But on the key issue of foreign ownership, over which the United States has been pressing hard, there was no change in Canada's position.
